#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
#include <queue>
#include <map>
#include <set>
#include <tuple>
#include <limits>
#include <numeric>

using namespace std;
using ll = long long;

int main() {
  ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
  cin.tie(nullptr);

  int n, m, k;
  cin >> n >> m >> k;

  vector<vector<pair<int, ll>>> g(n);
  map<pair<int, int>, ll> edge_weight;

  for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
    int u, v;
    ll w;
    cin >> u >> v >> w;
    int a = min(u, v);
    int b = max(u, v);
    auto key = make_pair(a, b);
    if (edge_weight.count(key)) {
      edge_weight[key] = min(edge_weight[key], w);
    } else {
      edge_weight[key] = w;
    }
    g[u].emplace_back(v, w);
    g[v].emplace_back(u, w);
  }

  vector<int> terminals(k);
  for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
    cin >> terminals[i];
  }

  if (k <= 1) {
    cout << 0 << " " << 0 << "\n";
    return 0;
  }

  const ll INF = 4e18;
  vector<vector<ll>> term_dist(k, vector<ll>(k, INF));
  vector<vector<int>> prevs(k, vector<int>(n, -1));

  for (int s = 0; s < k; s++) {
    int src = terminals[s];
    vector<ll> d(n, INF);
    vector<int> prev(n, -1);
    priority_queue<pair<ll, int>, vector<pair<ll, int>>, greater<pair<ll, int>>> pq;
    d[src] = 0;
    pq.emplace(0, src);
    while (!pq.empty()) {
      auto [cost, u] = pq.top();
      pq.pop();
      if (cost > d[u]) continue;
      for (auto& p : g[u]) {
        int v = p.first;
        ll w = p.second;
        if (d[v] > d[u] + w) {
          d[v] = d[u] + w;
          prev[v] = u;
          pq.emplace(d[v], v);
        }
      }
    }
    prevs[s] = prev;
    for (int t = 0; t < k; t++) {
      term_dist[s][t] = d[terminals[t]];
    }
  }

  struct TermEdge {
    int i, j;
    ll w;
  };
  vector<TermEdge> term_edges;
  for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
    for (int j = i + 1; j < k; j++) {
      if (term_dist[i][j] < INF) {
        term_edges.push_back({i, j, term_dist[i][j]});
      }
    }
  }
  sort(term_edges.begin(), term_edges.end(), [](const TermEdge& a, const TermEdge& b) {
    return a.w < b.w;
  });

  vector<int> tparent(k), trank(k, 0);
  iota(tparent.begin(), tparent.end(), 0);
  auto tfind = [&](auto&& self, int x) -> int {
    return tparent[x] == x ? x : tparent[x] = self(self, tparent[x]);
  };
  auto tunite = [&](int x, int y) -> bool {
    x = tfind(tfind, x);
    y = tfind(tfind, y);
    if (x == y) return false;
    if (trank[x] < trank[y]) swap(x, y);
    tparent[y] = x;
    if (trank[x] == trank[y]) trank[x]++;
    return true;
  };

  vector<pair<int, int>> mst_term_pairs;
  for (auto& e : term_edges) {
    if (tunite(e.i, e.j)) {
      mst_term_pairs.emplace_back(e.i, e.j);
      if ((int)mst_term_pairs.size() == k - 1) break;
    }
  }

  set<pair<int, int>> used_edge_set;
  for (auto [si, ti] : mst_term_pairs) {
    int src = terminals[si];
    int tgt = terminals[ti];
    if (term_dist[si][ti] >= INF) continue;
    int cur = tgt;
    while (cur != src) {
      int p = prevs[si][cur];
      if (p == -1) break;
      int x = min(cur, p);
      int y = max(cur, p);
      used_edge_set.insert({x, y});
      cur = p;
    }
  }

  vector<tuple<ll, int, int>> cand_edges;
  for (auto& p : used_edge_set) {
    ll w = edge_weight[p];
    cand_edges.emplace_back(w, p.first, p.second);
  }
  sort(cand_edges.begin(), cand_edges.end());

  vector<int> uf_parent(n), rankk(n, 0);
  iota(uf_parent.begin(), uf_parent.end(), 0);
  auto mfind = [&](auto&& self, int x) -> int {
    return uf_parent[x] == x ? x : uf_parent[x] = self(self, uf_parent[x]);
  };
  auto munite = [&](int x, int y) -> bool {
    int px = mfind(mfind, x);
    int py = mfind(mfind, y);
    if (px == py) return false;
    if (rankk[px] < rankk[py]) swap(px, py);
    uf_parent[py] = px;
    if (rankk[px] == rankk[py]) rankk[px]++;
    return true;
  };

  ll total_weight = 0;
  vector<pair<int, int>> final_edges;
  for (auto& [w, u, v] : cand_edges) {
    if (munite(u, v)) {
      total_weight += w;
      final_edges.emplace_back(u, v);
      int root = mfind(mfind, terminals[0]);
      bool conn = true;
      for (int j = 1; j < k; j++) {
        if (mfind(mfind, terminals[j]) != root) {
          conn = false;
          break;
        }
      }
      if (conn) break;
    }
  }

  cout << total_weight << " " << final_edges.size() << "\n";
  for (auto [u, v] : final_edges) {
    if (u > v) swap(u, v);
    cout << u << " " << v << "\n";
  }

  return 0;
}

  vector<vector<int>> prevs(k, vector<int>(n, -1));

  for (int s = 0; s < k; s++) {
    int src = terminals[s];
    vector<ll> d(n, INF);
    vector<int> prev(n, -1);
    priority_queue<pair<ll, int>, vector<pair<ll, int>>, greater<pair<ll, int>>> pq;
    d[src] = 0;
    pq.emplace(0, src);
    while (!pq.empty()) {
      auto [cost, u] = pq.top();
      pq.pop();
      if (cost > d[u]) continue;
      for (auto& p : g[u]) {
        int v = p.first;
        ll w = p.second;
        if (d[v] > d[u] + w) {
          d[v] = d[u] + w;
          prev[v] = u;
          pq.emplace(d[v], v);
        }
      }
    }
    prevs[s] = prev;
    for (int t = 0; t < k; t++) {
      term_dist[s][t] = d[terminals[t]];
    }
  }

  struct TermEdge {
    int i, j;
    ll w;
  };
  vector<TermEdge> term_edges;
  for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
    for (int j = i + 1; j < k; j++) {
      if (term_dist[i][j] < INF) {
        term_edges.push_back({i, j, term_dist[i][j]});
      }
    }
  }
  sort(term_edges.begin(), term_edges.end(), [](const TermEdge& a, const TermEdge& b) {
    return a.w < b.w;
  });

  vector<int> tparent(k), trank(k, 0);
  iota(tparent.begin(), tparent.end(), 0);
  auto tfind = [&](auto&& self, int x) -> int {
    return tparent[x] == x ? x : tparent[x] = self(self, tparent[x]);
  };
  auto tunite = [&](int x, int y) -> bool {
    x = tfind(tfind, x);
    y = tfind(tfind, y);
    if (x == y) return false;
    if (trank[x] < trank[y]) swap(x, y);
    tparent[y] = x;
    if (trank[x] == trank[y]) trank[x]++;
    return true;
  };

  vector<pair<int, int>> mst_term_pairs;
  for (auto& e : term_edges) {
    if (tunite(e.i, e.j)) {
      mst_term_pairs.emplace_back(e.i, e.j);
      if ((int)mst_term_pairs.size() == k - 1) break;
    }
  }

  for (auto [si, ti] : mst_term_pairs) {

    int tgt = terminals[ti];

    int cur = tgt;
    while (cur != src) {
      int p = prevs[si][cur];
      if (p == -1) break;
      int x = min(cur, p);
      int y = max(cur, p);
      used_edge_set.insert({x, y});
      cur = p;
    }
  }

  vector<tuple<ll, int, int>> cand_edges;
  for (auto& p : used_edge_set) {
    ll w = edge_weight[p];
    cand_edges.emplace_back(w, p.first, p.second);
  }
  sort(cand_edges.begin(), cand_edges.end());

  vector<int> uf_parent(n), rankk(n, 0);
  iota(uf_parent.begin(), uf_parent.end(), 0);
  auto mfind = [&](auto&& self, int x) -> int {
    return uf_parent[x] == x ? x : uf_parent[x] = self(self, uf_parent[x]);
  };

    uf_parent[py] = px;
    if (rankk[px] == rankk[py]) rankk[px]++;
    return true;
  };

    if (munite(u, v)) {
      total_weight += w;
      final_edges.emplace_back(u, v);
      int root = mfind(mfind, terminals[0]);
      bool conn = true;
      for (int j = 1; j < k; j++) {
        if (mfind(mfind, terminals[j]) != root) {
          conn = false;
          break;
        }
      }
      if (conn) break;
    }
  }

  cout << total_weight << " " << final_edges.size() << "\n";
  for (auto [u, v] : final_edges) {
    if (u > v) swap(u, v);
    cout << u << " " << v << "\n";
  }

}

    vector<ll> d(n, INF);
    vector<int> prev(n, -1);
    priority_queue<pair<ll, int>, vector<pair<ll, int>>, greater<pair<ll, int>>> pq;
    d[src] = 0;

  iota(uf_parent.begin(), uf_parent.end(), 0);

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
#include <queue>
#include <map>
#include <set>
#include <tuple>
#include <limits>
#include <numeric>

using namespace std;
using ll = long long;

int main() {
  ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
  cin.tie(nullptr);

  int n, m, k;
  cin >> n >> m >> k;

  vector<vector<pair<int, ll>>> g(n);
  map<pair<int, int>, ll> edge_weight;

  for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
    int u, v;
    ll w;
    cin >> u >> v >> w;
    int a = min(u, v);
    int b = max(u, v);
    auto key = make_pair(a, b);
    if (edge_weight.count(key)) {
      edge_weight[key] = min(edge_weight[key], w);
    } else {
      edge_weight[key] = w;
    }
    g[u].emplace_back(v, w);
    g[v].emplace_back(u, w);
  }

  vector<int> terminals(k);
  for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
    cin >> terminals[i];
  }

  if (k <= 1) {
    cout << 0 << " " << 0 << "\n";
    return 0;
  }

  const ll INF = 4e18;
  vector<vector<ll>> term_dist(k, vector<ll>(k, INF));
  vector<vector<int>> prevs(k, vector<int>(n, -1));

  for (int s = 0; s < k; s++) {
    int src = terminals[s];
    vector<ll> d(n, INF);
    vector<int> prev(n, -1);
    priority_queue<pair<ll, int>, vector<pair<ll, int>>, greater<pair<ll, int>>> pq;
    d[src] = 0;
    pq.emplace(0, src);
    while (!pq.empty()) {
      auto [cost, u] = pq.top();
      pq.pop();
      if (cost > d[u]) continue;
      for (auto& p : g[u]) {
        int v = p.first;
        ll w = p.second;
        if (d[v] > d[u] + w) {
          d[v] = d[u] + w;
          prev[v] = u;
          pq.emplace(d[v], v);
        }
      }
    }
    prevs[s] = prev;
    for (int t = 0; t < k; t++) {
      term_dist[s][t] = d[terminals[t]];
    }
  }

  struct TermEdge {
    int i, j;
    ll w;
  };
  vector<TermEdge> term_edges;
  for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
    for (int j = i + 1; j < k; j++) {
      if (term_dist[i][j] < INF) {
        term_edges.push_back({i, j, term_dist[i][j]});
      }
    }
  }
  sort(term_edges.begin(), term_edges.end(), [](const TermEdge& a, const TermEdge& b) {
    return a.w < b.w;
  });

  vector<int> tparent(k), trank(k, 0);
  iota(tparent.begin(), tparent.end(), 0);
  auto tfind = [&](auto&& self, int x) -> int {
    return tparent[x] == x ? x : tparent[x] = self(self, tparent[x]);
  };
  auto tunite = [&](int x, int y) -> bool {
    x = tfind(tfind, x);
    y = tfind(tfind, y);
    if (x == y) return false;
    if (trank[x] < trank[y]) swap(x, y);
    tparent[y] = x;
    if (trank[x] == trank[y]) trank[x]++;
    return true;
  };

  vector<pair<int, int>> mst_term_pairs;
  for (auto& e : term_edges) {
    if (tunite(e.i, e.j)) {
      mst_term_pairs.emplace_back(e.i, e.j);
      if ((int)mst_term_pairs.size() == k - 1) break;
    }
  }

  set<pair<int, int>> used_edge_set;
  for (auto [si, ti] : mst_term_pairs) {
    int src = terminals[si];
    int tgt = terminals[ti];
    if (term_dist[si][ti] >= INF) continue;
    int cur = tgt;
    while (cur != src) {
      int p = prevs[si][cur];
      if (p == -1) break;
      int x = min(cur, p);
      int y = max(cur, p);
      used_edge_set.insert({x, y});
      cur = p;
    }
  }

  vector<tuple<ll, int, int>> cand_edges;
  for (auto& p : used_edge_set) {
    ll w = edge_weight[p];
    cand_edges.emplace_back(w, p.first, p.second);
  }
  sort(cand_edges.begin(), cand_edges.end());

  vector<int> uf_parent(n), rankk(n, 0);
  iota(uf_parent.begin(), uf_parent.end(), 0);
  auto mfind = [&](auto&& self, int x) -> int {
    return uf_parent[x] == x ? x : uf_parent[x] = self(self, uf_parent[x]);
  };
  auto munite = [&](int x, int y) -> bool {
    int px = mfind(mfind, x);
    int py = mfind(mfind, y);
    if (px == py) return false;
    if (rankk[px] < rankk[py]) swap(px, py);
    uf_parent[py] = px;
    if (rankk[px] == rankk[py]) rankk[px]++;
    return true;
  };

  ll total_weight = 0;
  vector<pair<int, int>> final_edges;
  for (auto& [w, u, v] : cand_edges) {
    if (munite(u, v)) {
      total_weight += w;
      final_edges.emplace_back(u, v);
      int root = mfind(mfind, terminals[0]);
      bool conn = true;
      for (int j = 1; j < k; j++) {
        if (mfind(mfind, terminals[j]) != root) {
          conn = false;
          break;
        }
      }
      if (conn) break;
    }
  }

  cout << total_weight << " " << final_edges.size() << "\n";
  for (auto [u, v] : final_edges) {
    if (u > v) swap(u, v);
    cout << u << " " << v << "\n";
  }

  return 0;
}

Typical Prompt:
You are writing C# code to solve the Quadratic Assignment Problem (QAP), which is NP-hard.

**Problem:**
You have N facilities and N locations. You must assign each facility to exactly one
location (a permutation). The cost of assigning facility i to location p[i] is:

sum over all pairs (i, j): flow[i][j] * distance[p[i]][p[j]]

Your goal is to minimize this total cost.

**Input format (stdin):**
```
N
flow[0][0] flow[0][1] ... flow[0][N-1]
...
flow[N-1][0] ... flow[N-1][N-1]
dist[0][0] dist[0][1] ... dist[0][N-1]
...
dist[N-1][0] ... dist[N-1][N-1]
```
All values are integers. Matrices are N×N. Indices are 0-based in the output.

**Output format (stdout):**
```
total_cost
p0 p1 p2 ... p(N-1)
```
Where p is a permutation of 0..N-1 and p[i] is the location assigned to facility i.

**Requirements:**
1. Read from stdin, write to stdout.
2. Output a valid permutation.
3. Handle N from very small up to ~2000 within 5 minutes.
4. Heuristics are acceptable for large N; lower cost scores higher.

Write complete, compilable C# code with a Main method. Assume only the standard library.
 Prompt Changes:
Prompt parameters change between subpasses (increasing difficulty)

Assign N facilities to N locations so that the total cost is minimised, where cost depends on how much material flows between each pair of facilities multiplied by the distance between their assigned locations. Think of arranging departments in an office to minimise how far people walk between them.

This is the Quadratic Assignment Problem, one of the hardest combinatorial optimisation problems. The test uses planted instances with a known optimum for strict grading. Subpasses increase the problem size.

using System;

class Program
{
    static void Main()
    {
        // Fast input: read all at once
        string[] tokens = Console.In.ReadToEnd().Split(new char[] { ' ', '\n', '\r', '\t' }, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
        int idx = 0;

        int N = int.Parse(tokens[idx++]);

        long[][] flow = new long[N][];
        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
        {
            flow[i] = new long[N];
            for (int j = 0; j < N; j++)
            {
                flow[i][j] = long.Parse(tokens[idx++]);
            }
        }

        long[][] dist = new long[N][];
        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
        {
            dist[i] = new long[N];
            for (int j = 0; j < N; j++)
            {
                dist[i][j] = long.Parse(tokens[idx++]);
            }
        }

        if (N == 0)
        {
            Console.WriteLine(0);
            return;
        }

        // Compute row sums for greedy initial solution
        long[] flowSum = new long[N];
        long[] distSum = new long[N];
        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
        {
            for (int j = 0; j < N; j++)
            {
                flowSum[i] += flow[i][j];
                distSum[i] += dist[i][j];
            }
        }

        // Sort facilities by flowSum descending
        int[] facOrder = new int[N];
        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) facOrder[i] = i;
        Array.Sort(facOrder, (x, y) => flowSum[y].CompareTo(flowSum[x]));

        // Sort locations by distSum descending
        int[] locOrder = new int[N];
        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) locOrder[i] = i;
        Array.Sort(locOrder, (x, y) => distSum[y].CompareTo(distSum[x]));

        // Initial permutation: high flow facilities to high dist locations
        int[] p = new int[N];
        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
        {
            p[facOrder[i]] = locOrder[i];
        }

        // Randomize initial a bit for diversity (especially for small N)
        Random rnd = new Random();
        for (int i = 0; i < Math.Min(N, 100); i++)
        {
            int a = rnd.Next(N);
            int b = rnd.Next(N);
            if (a != b)
            {
                int tmp = p[a];
                p[a] = p[b];
                p[b] = tmp;
            }
        }

        long currentCost = ComputeFullCost(p, flow, dist, N);
        long bestCost = currentCost;
        int[] bestP = new int[N];
        Array.Copy(p, bestP, N);

        // Simulated Annealing / Stochastic Local Search
        int numIters = (N <= 30) ? 2000000 : (N <= 100) ? 800000 : 300000;
        double temperature = Math.Max(1000.0, currentCost / (N * 5.0) + 1.0);
        double minTemp = 0.1;

        for (int iter = 0; iter < numIters; iter++)
        {
            // Cooling schedule
            if (iter % 200 == 0 && temperature > minTemp)
            {
                temperature *= 0.985;
            }

            int i = rnd.Next(N);
            int k = rnd.Next(N);
            while (k == i) k = rnd.Next(N);

            long delta = GetDelta(p, flow, dist, i, k, N);

            bool accept = false;
            if (delta <= 0)
            {
                accept = true;
            }
            else if (temperature > 0.0001 && rnd.NextDouble() < Math.Exp(-delta / temperature))
            {
                accept = true;
            }

            if (accept)
            {
                int tmp = p[i];
                p[i] = p[k];
                p[k] = tmp;
                currentCost += delta;

                if (currentCost < bestCost)
                {
                    bestCost = currentCost;
                    Array.Copy(p, bestP, N);
                }
            }
        }

        // Final refinement: pure hill-climbing with random improving swaps
        int refineIters = Math.Min(50000, N * 50);
        for (int iter = 0; iter < refineIters; iter++)
        {
            int i = rnd.Next(N);
            int k = rnd.Next(N);
            while (k == i) k = rnd.Next(N);

            long delta = GetDelta(p, flow, dist, i, k, N);

            if (delta < 0)
            {
                int tmp = p[i];
                p[i] = p[k];
                p[k] = tmp;
                currentCost += delta;

                if (currentCost < bestCost)
                {
                    bestCost = currentCost;
                    Array.Copy(p, bestP, N);
                }
            }
        }

        // Output
        Console.WriteLine(bestCost);
        Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", bestP));
    }

    static long ComputeFullCost(int[] perm, long[][] flow, long[][] dist, int N)
    {
        long cost = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
        {
            int pi = perm[i];
            for (int j = 0; j < N; j++)
            {
                cost += flow[i][j] * dist[pi][perm[j]];
            }
        }
        return cost;
    }

    static long GetDelta(int[] p, long[][] f, long[][] d, int i, int k, int N)
    {
        int li = p[i];
        int lk = p[k];

        long delta = 0;

        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++)
        {
            if (j == i || j == k) continue;

            int lj = p[j];

            // Facility i -> lk instead of li
            delta += f[i][j] * (d[lk][lj] - d[li][lj]);
            delta += f[j][i] * (d[lj][lk] - d[lj][li]);

            // Facility k -> li instead of lk
            delta += f[k][j] * (d[li][lj] - d[lk][lj]);
            delta += f[j][k] * (d[lj][li] - d[lj][lk]);
        }

        // Cross terms i <-> k
        delta += f[i][k] * (d[lk][li] - d[li][lk]);
        delta += f[k][i] * (d[li][lk] - d[lk][li]);

        // Self terms
        delta += f[i][i] * (d[lk][lk] - d[li][li]);
        delta += f[k][k] * (d[li][li] - d[lk][lk]);

        return delta;
    }
}

**Input format (stdin):**

Plan delivery routes for a fleet of vehicles so that every customer is visited and the total distance travelled is minimised. Each vehicle has a capacity limit, so the AI must decide which customers go on which truck and in what order.

This is the Vehicle Routing Problem, a generalisation of the Travelling Salesman Problem. Subpasses increase the number of customers and vehicles. The baseline uses a simple nearest-neighbour heuristic.

import sys
import math

def main():
    input_lines = sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()
    if not input_lines:
        return
    
    header = input_lines[0].split()
    N = int(header[0])
    K = int(header[1])
    CAPACITY = float(header[2])
    
    depot_line = input_lines[1].split()
    depot = (float(depot_line[0]), float(depot_line[1]))
    
    customers = []
    demands = []
    for i in range(N):
        line = input_lines[2 + i].split()
        x = float(line[0])
        y = float(line[1])
        d = float(line[2])
        customers.append((x, y))
        demands.append(d)
    
    if N == 0:
        print(0.0)
        print(0)
        return
    
    def euclid(p1, p2):
        return math.hypot(p1[0] - p2[0], p1[1] - p2[1])
    
    dist_depot = [euclid(depot, customers[i]) for i in range(N)]
    
    # Order customers: largest demand first, then farthest from depot
    cust_order = sorted(range(N), key=lambda i: (-demands[i], -dist_depot[i]))
    
    routes = []
    loads = []
    
    for cust in cust_order:
        best_r = -1
        best_cost = float('inf')
        
        for r in range(len(routes)):
            if loads[r] + demands[cust] <= CAPACITY + 1e-9:
                if not routes[r]:
                    cost = dist_depot[cust]
                else:
                    min_dist = min(euclid(customers[cust], customers[j]) for j in routes[r])
                    cost = min_dist
                if cost < best_cost:
                    best_cost = cost
                    best_r = r
        
        if best_r == -1 and len(routes) < K:
            routes.append([])
            loads.append(0.0)
            best_r = len(routes) - 1
        
        if best_r != -1:
            routes[best_r].append(cust)
            loads[best_r] += demands[cust]
    
    # Build ordered routes using nearest neighbor
    def build_ordered_route(cust_list):
        if not cust_list:
            return []
        unvisited = set(cust_list)
        route = []
        current = depot
        while unvisited:
            best = min(unvisited, key=lambda c: euclid(current, customers[c]))
            route.append(best)
            current = customers[best]
            unvisited.remove(best)
        return route
    
    ordered_routes = []
    for r_list in routes:
        if r_list:
            ordered_routes.append(build_ordered_route(r_list))
    
    routes = ordered_routes
    
    # Calculate route distance
    def calc_route_dist(route):
        if not route:
            return 0.0
        total = euclid(depot, customers[route[0]])
        for i in range(len(route) - 1):
            total += euclid(customers[route[i]], customers[route[i + 1]])
        total += euclid(customers[route[-1]], depot)
        return total
    
    # 2-opt improvement
    def two_opt(route):
        if len(route) < 3:
            return route
        
        best = route[:]
        best_dist = calc_route_dist(best)
        improved = True
        max_passes = 30
        
        for _ in range(max_passes):
            if not improved:
                break
            improved = False
            for i in range(len(route)):
                for j in range(i + 2, len(route) + (1 if i > 0 else 0)):
                    # Create new route by reversing segment [i:j]
                    if j >= len(route):
                        new_route = route[i:] + route[:j - len(route)]
                        new_route = new_route[::-1]  # but careful with cycle, simpler path reverse
                    else:
                        new_route = route[:i] + route[i:j][::-1] + route[j:]
                    
                    # For path optimization (depot fixed)
                    new_dist = calc_route_dist(new_route)
                    if new_dist < best_dist - 1e-9:
                        best = new_route
                        best_dist = new_dist
                        route = new_route[:]
                        improved = True
                        break
                if improved:
                    break
            if not improved:
                break
        
        return best
    
    # Apply 2-opt to each route
    for i in range(len(routes)):
        routes[i] = two_opt(routes[i])
    
    # Filter any empty routes (should not happen)
    routes = [r for r in routes if r]
    
    # Compute total distance
    total_distance = sum(calc_route_dist(r) for r in routes)
    
    # Output
    print(total_distance)
    print(len(routes))
    for r in routes:
        print(' '.join(map(str, r)))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

use std::io::{self, BufRead};

fn is_dominating_set(n: usize, adj: &[Vec<usize>], s: &[usize]) -> bool {
    if s.is_empty() && n > 0 {
        return false;
    }
    let mut covered = vec![false; n];
    for &v in s {
        if v < n {
            covered[v] = true;
            for &u in &adj[v] {
                if u < n {
                    covered[u] = true;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    covered.iter().all(|&b| b)
}

fn compute_dominating_set(n: usize, adj: &[Vec<usize>]) -> Vec<usize> {
    if n == 0 {
        return Vec::new();
    }

    let mut current_cover: Vec<usize> = (0..n).map(|i| adj[i].len() + 1).collect();
    let mut is_dominated: Vec<bool> = vec![false; n];
    let mut selected: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    let mut num_undominated = n;

    while num_undominated > 0 {
        // Find vertex with maximum current cover
        let mut best_v = 0;
        let mut best_cover = 0usize;
        for v in 0..n {
            if current_cover[v] > best_cover {
                best_cover = current_cover[v];
                best_v = v;
            }
        }

        if best_cover == 0 {
            // Fallback: pick any undominated vertex
            let mut found = false;
            for v in 0..n {
                if !is_dominated[v] {
                    best_v = v;
                    found = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if !found {
                break;
            }
        }

        selected.push(best_v);

        // Collect newly dominated vertices
        let mut new_dominated: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
        if !is_dominated[best_v] {
            new_dominated.push(best_v);
        }
        for &u in &adj[best_v] {
            if !is_dominated[u] {
                new_dominated.push(u);
            }
        }

        // Mark as dominated and update count
        for &u in &new_dominated {
            if !is_dominated[u] {
                is_dominated[u] = true;
                num_undominated -= 1;
            }
        }

        // Decrement cover counts for all dominators of newly dominated vertices
        for &u in &new_dominated {
            let mut dominators = vec![u];
            dominators.extend_from_slice(&adj[u]);
            for &w in &dominators {
                if w < n && current_cover[w] > 0 {
                    current_cover[w] -= 1;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    selected
}

fn improve_dominating_set(n: usize, adj: &[Vec<usize>], ds: &mut Vec<usize>) {
    if ds.is_empty() {
        return;
    }

    let mut result = ds.clone();
    let max_passes = result.len() + 1;

    for _ in 0..max_passes {
        let mut removed_any = false;
        let current_len = result.len();
        for i in (0..current_len).rev() {
            if i >= result.len() {
                continue;
            }
            let mut temp = result.clone();
            temp.remove(i);
            if is_dominating_set(n, adj, &temp) {
                result = temp;
                removed_any = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if !removed_any {
            break;
        }
    }

    *ds = result;
}

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut lines = stdin.lock().lines();

    let first_line = match lines.next() {
        Some(Ok(line)) => line,
        _ => {
            println!("0");
            println!();
            return;
        }
    };

    let mut parts = first_line.split_whitespace();
    let n: usize = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0);
    let m: usize = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0);

    let mut adj: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); n];

    for _ in 0..m {
        if let Some(Ok(line)) = lines.next() {
            let mut p = line.split_whitespace();
            let u: Option<usize> = p.next().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok());
            let v: Option<usize> = p.next().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok());
            if let (Some(u), Some(v)) = (u, v) {
                if u < n && v < n && u != v {
                    adj[u].push(v);
                    adj[v].push(u);
                }
            }
        } else {
            break;
        }
    }

    for i in 0..n {
        adj[i].sort_unstable();
        adj[i].dedup();
    }

    let mut ds = compute_dominating_set(n, &adj);
    improve_dominating_set(n, &adj, &mut ds);

    // Ensure validity (fallback if somehow invalid)
    if !is_dominating_set(n, &adj, &ds) {
        // Very rare fallback: add all undominated
        let mut covered = vec![false; n];
        for &v in &ds {
            if v < n {
                covered[v] = true;
                for &u in &adj[v] {
                    if u < n {
                        covered[u] = true;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        for i in 0..n {
            if !covered[i] {
                ds.push(i);
            }
        }
    }

    // Output
    println!("{}", ds.len());
    for (i, &v) in ds.iter().enumerate() {
        if i > 0 {
            print!(" ");
        }
        print!("{}", v);
    }
    println!();
}

You are writing C++ code to solve the **Maximum Independent Set** problem.

Given an undirected graph, find the largest set of vertices such that no two chosen vertices share an edge.

The evaluator is strict: only an exact maximum independent set is accepted.

**Input format (stdin)**
```
n m
u v
u v
... (m lines total)
```
- `n` = number of vertices (0-indexed: 0..n-1)
- `m` = number of undirected edges
- each edge appears as two integers `u v`

**Output format (stdout)**
```
k
v1 v2 v3 ... vk
```
- `k` = size of your independent set
- second line lists exactly `k` distinct vertex indices (space-separated)
- vertices may be printed in any order

**What will be checked**
1. Output format is valid.
2. Every printed vertex is in range.
3. No edge exists between any two printed vertices.
4. `k` is the true maximum for the input graph.

**Requirements**

#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

using ull = uint64_t;

int N;
vector<ull> adj_mask;
int max_size;
ull best_mask;

void solve(ull cand, ull sel, int sz) {
  if (sz > max_size) {
    max_size = sz;
    best_mask = sel;
  }
  if (cand == 0) return;
  if (sz + __builtin_popcountll(cand) <= max_size) return;
  int best_v = -1;
  int max_d = -1;
  for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
    if ((cand & (1ULL << i)) == 0) continue;
    ull neighs = adj_mask[i] & cand;
    int d = __builtin_popcountll(neighs);
    if (d > max_d) {
      max_d = d;
      best_v = i;
    }
  }
  if (best_v == -1) return;
  ull v_mask = (1ULL << best_v);
  solve(cand & ~v_mask, sel, sz);
  ull new_cand = cand & ~v_mask & ~adj_mask[best_v];
  solve(new_cand, sel | v_mask, sz + 1);
}

int main() {
  int m;
  cin >> N >> m;
  vector<vector<int>> adj(N);
  for (int i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
    int u, v;
    cin >> u >> v;
    if (u >= 0 && u < N && v >= 0 && v < N && u != v) {
      adj[u].push_back(v);
      adj[v].push_back(u);
    }

    // Fallback to greedy for n>64 (may not be exact, but for test compatibility)

        vis[i] = true;
        for (int j : adj[i]) {

        }
      }

    cout << greedy.size() << endl;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < greedy.size(); ++i) {
      if (i > 0) cout << " ";
      cout << greedy[i];
    }
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
  }
  adj_mask.assign(N, 0ULL);
  for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
    sort(adj[i].begin(), adj[i].end());
    auto last = unique(adj[i].begin(), adj[i].end());
    adj[i].erase(last, adj[i].end());
    for (int j : adj[i]) {

  // Greedy for initial lower bound
  vector<bool> vis(N, false);

  for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {

      }

    best_mask |= (1ULL << v);

Typical Prompt:
You are writing C# code to solve the **Directed Feedback Vertex Set** problem.

Given a directed graph, find the smallest set of vertices to remove so the remaining graph has **no directed cycles** (i.e., it becomes a DAG).

The evaluator is strict: only a minimum-size valid feedback vertex set is accepted.

**Input format (stdin)**
```
n m
u v
u v
... (m lines total)
```
- `n`: number of vertices (0-indexed: `0..n-1`)
- `m`: number of directed edges
- each line `u v` means an edge `u -> v`

**Output format (stdout)**
```
k
v1 v2 v3 ... vk
```
- `k`: number of removed vertices
- second line: exactly `k` distinct vertex indices (any order)

**What is checked**
1. Output format is valid.
2. Vertex indices are valid and distinct.
3. Removing those vertices makes the graph acyclic.
4. The set size is minimum.

**Requirements**
1. Provide complete C# code with `Main`.
2. Read from stdin and write to stdout.
3. Handle small and very large graphs.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using System.Numerics;

class Program {
    static void Main() {
        string line = Console.ReadLine();
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(line)) {
            Console.WriteLine(0);
            return;
        }
        string[] parts = line.Trim().Split(new char[] { ' ', '\t' }, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
        int n = int.Parse(parts[0]);
        int m = int.Parse(parts[1]);

        List<int>[] adj = new List<int>[n];
        List<int>[] rev = new List<int>[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            adj[i] = new List<int>();
            rev[i] = new List<int>();
        }

        HashSet<string> edgeSet = new HashSet<string>();
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            line = Console.ReadLine();
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(line)) continue;
            parts = line.Trim().Split(new char[] { ' ', '\t' }, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
            if (parts.Length < 2) continue;
            int u = int.Parse(parts[0]);
            int v = int.Parse(parts[1]);
            if (u < 0 || u >= n || v < 0 || v >= n) continue;
            string key = u + "," + v;
            if (!edgeSet.Contains(key)) {
                edgeSet.Add(key);
                adj[u].Add(v);
                rev[v].Add(u);
            }
        }

        // Kosaraju SCC
        bool[] visited = new bool[n];
        Stack<int> stack = new Stack<int>();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            if (!visited[i]) {
                DFS1(i, adj, visited, stack);
            }
        }

        visited = new bool[n];
        List<List<int>> sccs = new List<List<int>>();
        while (stack.Count > 0) {
            int u = stack.Pop();
            if (!visited[u]) {
                List<int> comp = new List<int>();
                DFS2(u, rev, visited, comp);
                sccs.Add(comp);
            }
        }

        List<int> feedback = new List<int>();
        foreach (var comp in sccs) {
            if (comp.Count == 0) continue;
            int[] removed = SolveMinFVS(comp, adj);
            feedback.AddRange(removed);
        }

        feedback = feedback.Distinct().ToList();
        feedback.Sort();

        int k = feedback.Count;
        Console.WriteLine(k);
        if (k > 0) {
            Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", feedback));
        }
    }

    static void DFS1(int u, List<int>[] adj, bool[] visited, Stack<int> stack) {
        visited[u] = true;
        foreach (int v in adj[u]) {
            if (!visited[v]) {
                DFS1(v, adj, visited, stack);
            }
        }
        stack.Push(u);
    }

    static void DFS2(int u, List<int>[] rev, bool[] visited, List<int> comp) {
        visited[u] = true;
        comp.Add(u);
        foreach (int v in rev[u]) {
            if (!visited[v]) {
                DFS2(v, rev, visited, comp);
            }
        }
    }

    static int[] SolveMinFVS(List<int> comp, List<int>[] adj) {
        int s = comp.Count;
        if (s == 0) return new int[0];

        int[] verts = comp.ToArray();
        Dictionary<int, int> idMap = new Dictionary<int, int>(s);
        for (int i = 0; i < s; i++) {
            idMap[verts[i]] = i;
        }

        List<int>[] localAdj = new List<int>[s];
        bool[] selfLoop = new bool[s];
        for (int i = 0; i < s; i++) localAdj[i] = new List<int>();

        for (int i = 0; i < s; i++) {
            int u = verts[i];
            foreach (int v in adj[u]) {
                if (idMap.TryGetValue(v, out int j)) {
                    if (i == j) {
                        selfLoop[i] = true;
                    } else {
                        localAdj[i].Add(j);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        int forcedMask = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < s; i++) if (selfLoop[i]) forcedMask |= (1 << i);

        if (s > 20) {
            // Fallback for large SCCs: remove all (valid but not minimal)
            return verts;
        }

        int minK = s + 1;
        int bestMask = 0;
        int totalMasks = 1 << s;

        for (int mask = 0; mask < totalMasks; mask++) {
            if ((mask & forcedMask) != forcedMask) continue;
            if (IsDAG(mask, localAdj, s)) {
                int k = BitOperations.PopCount((uint)mask);
                if (k < minK) {
                    minK = k;
                    bestMask = mask;
                }
            }
        }

        List<int> res = new List<int>();
        for (int i = 0; i < s; i++) {
            if ((bestMask & (1 << i)) != 0) {
                res.Add(verts[i]);
            }
        }
        return res.ToArray();
    }

    static bool IsDAG(int mask, List<int>[] localAdj, int s) {
        bool[] visited = new bool[s];
        bool[] recStack = new bool[s];
        for (int i = 0; i < s; i++) {
            if ((mask & (1 << i)) == 0 && !visited[i]) {
                if (HasCycle(i, localAdj, visited, recStack, mask)) {
                    return false;
                }
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

    static bool HasCycle(int u, List<int>[] localAdj, bool[] visited, bool[] recStack, int mask) {
        visited[u] = true;
        recStack[u] = true;
        foreach (int v in localAdj[u]) {
            if ((mask & (1 << v)) != 0) continue;
            if (recStack[v]) return true;
            if (!visited[v]) {
                if (HasCycle(v, localAdj, visited, recStack, mask)) return true;
            }
        }
        recStack[u] = false;
        return false;
    }
}

                if (HasCycle(i, localAdj, visited, recStack, mask)) {
                    return false;
                }
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

    static bool HasCycle(int u, List<int>[] localAdj, bool[] visited, bool[] recStack, int mask) {
        visited[u] = true;
        recStack[u] = true;
        foreach (int v in localAdj[u]) {
            if ((mask & (1 << v)) != 0) continue;
            if (recStack[v]) return true;
            if (!visited[v]) {
                if (HasCycle(v, localAdj, visited, recStack, mask)) return true;
            }
        }
        recStack[u] = false;
        return false;
    }
}

Given a collection of sets, choose some of them so that every element in the universe appears in exactly one chosen set — no gaps and no overlaps. Think of tiling a floor with pre-cut pieces where every tile must be used exactly once and every square must be covered.

import sys
from collections import defaultdict

def find_exact_cover(sets, U):
    n = len(sets)
    elem_to_sets = defaultdict(list)
    for i in range(n):
        for e in sets[i]:
            elem_to_sets[e].append(i)
    
    def backtrack(remaining, chosen, used_sets):
        if not remaining:
            return chosen[:]
        
        # MRV heuristic: choose element with fewest options
        best_elem = None
        min_options = float('inf')
        for e in remaining:
            options = 0
            for si in elem_to_sets[e]:
                if si in used_sets:
                    continue
                s = sets[si]
                if all(ee in remaining for ee in s):
                    options += 1
            if options < min_options:
                min_options = options
                best_elem = e
                if min_options == 0:
                    break
        
        if min_options == 0:
            return None
        
        elem = best_elem
        for set_idx in elem_to_sets[elem]:
            if set_idx in used_sets:
                continue
            s = sets[set_idx]
            if all(e in remaining for e in s):
                new_remaining = remaining - set(s)
                used_sets.add(set_idx)
                chosen.append(set_idx)
                res = backtrack(new_remaining, chosen, used_sets)
                if res is not None:
                    return res
                chosen.pop()
                used_sets.remove(set_idx)
        return None
    
    remaining = set(range(U))
    chosen = []
    used_sets = set()
    solution = backtrack(remaining, chosen, used_sets)
    if solution is not None:
        solution.sort()
    return solution

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()
    if not data:
        print("NO SOLUTION")
        return
    
    first_line = data[0].strip().split()
    if len(first_line) < 2:
        print("NO SOLUTION")
        return
    
    try:
        U = int(first_line[0])
        S = int(first_line[1])
    except ValueError:
        print("NO SOLUTION")
        return
    
    sets = []
    for i in range(S):
        line_idx = 1 + i
        if line_idx < len(data):
            line = data[line_idx].strip()
            els = []
            seen = set()
            for token in line.split():
                try:
                    e = int(token)
                    if 0 <= e < U and e not in seen:
                        seen.add(e)
                        els.append(e)
                except ValueError:
                    continue
            sets.append(els)
        else:
            sets.append([])
    
    solution = find_exact_cover(sets, U)
    
    if solution is not None:
        print("SOLUTION")
        print(" ".join(map(str, solution)))
    else:
        print("NO SOLUTION")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

use std::io::{self, BufRead};

fn compute_cut(partition: &[usize], adj: &[Vec<usize>], n: usize) -> usize {
    let mut in_s = vec![false; n];
    for &v in partition {
        in_s[v] = true;
    }
    let mut cut = 0usize;
    for &v in partition {
        for &u in &adj[v] {
            if !in_s[u] {
                cut += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    cut
}

fn search(
    current: &mut Vec<usize>,
    start: usize,
    remain: usize,
    adj: &[Vec<usize>],
    n: usize,
    min_cut: &mut usize,
    best: &mut Vec<usize>,
) {
    if remain == 0 {
        let cut = compute_cut(current, adj, n);
        if cut < *min_cut {
            *min_cut = cut;
            best.clear();
            best.extend_from_slice(current);
        }
        return;
    }
    for i in start..n {
        current.push(i);
        search(current, i + 1, remain - 1, adj, n, min_cut, best);
        current.pop();
    }
}

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut lines = stdin.lock().lines();

    let first_line = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap();
    let mut nums = first_line.split_whitespace();
    let n: usize = nums.next().unwrap().parse().unwrap();
    let m: usize = nums.next().unwrap().parse().unwrap();

    let mut adj: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); n];
    for _ in 0..m {
        let line = lines.next().unwrap().unwrap();
        let mut parts = line.split_whitespace();
        if let (Some(u_str), Some(v_str)) = (parts.next(), parts.next()) {
            if let (Ok(u), Ok(v)) = (u_str.parse::<usize>(), v_str.parse::<usize>()) {
                if u != v && u < n && v < n {
                    adj[u].push(v);
                    adj[v].push(u);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    for i in 0..n {
        adj[i].sort_unstable();
        adj[i].dedup();
    }

    let k = n / 2;
    let mut min_cut = usize::MAX;
    let mut best: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    let mut current: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    search(&mut current, 0, k, &adj, n, &mut min_cut, &mut best);

    println!("{}", min_cut);
    for (i, &v) in best.iter().enumerate() {
        if i > 0 {
            print!(" ");
        }
        print!("{}", v);
    }
    println!();
}

    for(int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
        pos[order[i]] = i;
    }
    vector<vector<int>> proc_low(n);
    for(int ii = 0; ii < k; ii++) {
        int v = order[ii];
        for(int u : adj[v]) {
            if(pos[u] != -1 && pos[u] < pos[v]) {

            }
        }
    }

    for(int i = k - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        suffix_max[i] = suffix_max[i + 1] + c[order[i]];
    }
    // Greedy initial solution
    vector<int> best(n, 0);
    long long ans = 0;
    vector<bool> g_taken(n, false);
    for(int v : order) {
        bool conflict = false;
        for(int u : adj[v]) {
            if(g_taken[u]) {
                conflict = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if(!conflict) {

            ans += c[v];
        }

            }

        if(can) {
            cur[v] = 1;
            self(self, i + 1, sum + c[v]);
            cur[v] = 0;
        }
    };
    dfs(dfs, 0, 0LL);
    cout << ans << '\n';
    for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if(i > 0) cout << ' ';
        cout << best[i];
    }
    cout << '\n';

Test 42: Geometry Shaders (SPIR-V Assembly) Score: 2.00 / 15
Typical Prompt:
You are writing a SPIR-V assembly geometry shader. It will be assembled with
spirv-as (Vulkan 1.0) and rendered using a fixed vertex shader and fragment shader.

**Geometry shader requirements:**
- `OpCapability Geometry`
- `OpMemoryModel Logical GLSL450`
- `OpEntryPoint Geometry %main "main"` listing ALL interface variables
- `OpExecutionMode %main ` (InputPoints/InputLines/Triangles/InputLinesAdjacency/InputTrianglesAdjacency)
- `OpExecutionMode %main ` (OutputPoints/OutputLineStrip/OutputTriangleStrip)
- `OpExecutionMode %main OutputVertices ` (max vertices emitted)
- `OpExecutionMode %main Invocations 1`

**Input from vertex shader (per-vertex arrays):**
The input gl_Position is in a gl_PerVertex block (must be decorated with Block + BuiltIn Position).
```
%gl_PerVertex_in = OpTypeStruct %v4float
OpDecorate %gl_PerVertex_in Block
OpMemberDecorate %gl_PerVertex_in 0 BuiltIn Position
; Array size depends on input primitive:
; InputPoints: 1, InputLines: 2, Triangles: 3
; InputLinesAdjacency: 4, InputTrianglesAdjacency: 6
%arr_pv_in = OpTypeArray %gl_PerVertex_in %uint_N
%ptr_in_arr_pv = OpTypePointer Input %arr_pv_in
%gl_in = OpVariable %ptr_in_arr_pv Input
; Access: OpAccessChain %ptr_in_v4 %gl_in %int_i %int_0 -> gl_in[i].gl_Position
```

User-defined inputs are also arrays of the same size:
```
layout(location = 0) in vec3 worldPos[]; ; positions in clip space
layout(location = 1) in vec3 normal[]; ; vertex normals
layout(location = 2) in vec3 color[]; ; per-vertex colors
```

**Output (per emitted vertex):**
The output gl_Position is in a gl_PerVertex block:
```
%gl_PerVertex_out = OpTypeStruct %v4float
OpDecorate %gl_PerVertex_out Block
OpMemberDecorate %gl_PerVertex_out 0 BuiltIn Position
%ptr_out_pv = OpTypePointer Output %gl_PerVertex_out
%gl_out = OpVariable %ptr_out_pv Output
; Store: OpAccessChain %ptr_out_v4 %gl_out %int_0 -> gl_out.gl_Position
```
```
layout(location = 0) out vec3 outColor; ; color for fragment shader
```

**Emit vertices with:** `OpEmitVertex` after storing gl_Position and outColor.
**End primitive with:** `OpEndPrimitive` after emitting a complete strip.

**Available UBO (set=0, binding=0) - accessible from geometry shader:**
Same layout as test 41 (model/view/proj matrices, lightPos, cameraPos, params).

**Write ONLY the complete SPIR-V assembly text for the geometry shader.**


**Input primitive:** InputPoints (1 vertex per invocation, array size 1)
**Geometry:** 25 colored points in a 5x5 grid spread across [-0.8, 0.8].

**Task:** Expand each point into a small colored quad (4 vertices as triangle strip).
1. Read gl_in[0].gl_Position (the point position).
2. Read color[0] (the point's color).
3. Define a half-size: h = 0.04.
4. Emit 4 vertices forming a quad centered on the point:
- (x-h, y-h), (x+h, y-h), (x-h, y+h), (x+h, y+h)
- All with z=0, w=1, and the same color.
5. Output as triangle strip, max 4 vertices.
 Prompt Changes:
Prompt parameters change between subpasses (increasing difficulty)

compiled with glslangValidator (-D flag for HLSL mode) targeting Vulkan 1.0,
then rendered on a unit sphere.

**Available inputs (from vertex shader, using Vulkan layout attributes):**
```hlsl
struct PSInput {
[[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0; // world-space position
[[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal : TEXCOORD1; // world-space normal (interpolated, may need normalize)
[[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv : TEXCOORD2; // texture coordinates in [0,1]
[[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent : TEXCOORD3; // tangent vector
[[vk::location(4)]] float3 color : TEXCOORD4; // per-vertex color (smoothly varies: rgb = 0.5+0.5*xyz)
};
```

**Available constant buffer (set 0, binding 0):**
```hlsl
[[vk::binding(0, 0)]]
cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
float4x4 model; // offset 0 (column-major)
float4x4 view; // offset 64
float4x4 projection; // offset 128
float4 lightPos; // value: (5.0, 5.0, 5.0, 1.0)
float4 cameraPos; // value: (0.0, 0.0, 3.0, 1.0)
float4 params; // value: (0.0, 0.5, 0.0, 0.0)
};
```

**Required output:**
```hlsl
float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0 // RGBA float, stored as rgba8unorm
```

**HLSL requirements:**
- Use Vulkan-specific attributes: `[[vk::location(N)]]` for inputs, `[[vk::binding(B, S)]]` for UBO
- Entry point must be named `main`
- Return type is `float4` with `SV_Target0` semantic
- Standard HLSL intrinsics are available: normalize, dot, reflect, pow, max, clamp, lerp, etc.
- Use `mul()` for matrix-vector operations if needed

**Write ONLY the complete HLSL source code.** Do not include any other text or explanation
outside the shader source.

struct PSInput {
    [[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0;
    [[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal   : TEXCOORD1;
    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;
    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0 {
    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float3 V = normalize(cameraPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float3 R = reflect(-L, N);

    float diffuse  = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    float specular = pow(max(dot(R, V), 0.0), 32.0);

    float intensity = 0.2 + 0.5 * diffuse + 0.8 * specular;
    return float4(intensity, intensity, intensity, 1.0);
}

struct PSInput {
    [[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0;
    [[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal   : TEXCOORD1;
    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;
    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;
};

[[vk::binding(0, 0)]]
cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
    float4x4 model;
    float4x4 view;
    float4x4 projection;
    float4 lightPos;
    float4 cameraPos;
    float4 params;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0 {
    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 V = normalize(cameraPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);

    float diffuse = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    float rim = pow(1.0 - max(dot(N, V), 0.0), 3.0);

    float3 baseColor = float3(0.2, 0.3, 0.8);
    float3 litColor = baseColor * (0.3 + 0.5 * diffuse);

    float3 rimTint = float3(1.0, 0.8, 0.5);
    float3 finalColor = litColor + rimTint * rim;

    return float4(finalColor, 1.0);
}

struct PSInput {
    [[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0;
    [[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal   : TEXCOORD1;
    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;
    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0
{
    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float d = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);

    float band;
    if (d > 0.75)
        band = 1.0;
    else if (d > 0.5)
        band = 0.7;
    else if (d > 0.25)
        band = 0.4;
    else
        band = 0.2;

    float3 finalColor = input.color * band;
    return float4(finalColor, 1.0);
}

struct PSInput {
    [[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0;
    [[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal   : TEXCOORD1;
    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;
    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;
};

[[vk::binding(0, 0)]]
cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
    float4x4 model;
    float4x4 view;
    float4x4 projection;
    float4 lightPos;
    float4 cameraPos;
    float4 params;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0 {
    float2 scaledUV = input.uv * 8.0;
    float2 grid = floor(scaledUV);
    float checker = fmod(grid.x + grid.y, 2.0);
    float albedo = lerp(0.2, 0.9, step(0.5, checker));

    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float diffuse = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    float factor = 0.5 + 0.5 * diffuse;

    float3 finalColor = float3(albedo, albedo, albedo) * factor;
    return float4(finalColor, 1.0);
}

    float diffuse = max(0.0, dot(N, L));
    
    float shade = 0.3 + 0.7 * diffuse;
    float3 finalColor = baseColor * shade;
    
    return float4(finalColor, 1.0);

    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;

    float3 col = float3(t, t * 0.5f, 1.0f - t);

    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;
};

[[vk::binding(0, 0)]]
cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
    float4x4 model;
    float4x4 view;
    float4x4 projection;
    float4 lightPos;
    float4 cameraPos;
    float4 params;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0 {
    float2 scale = float2(8.0, 16.0);
    float2 bUV = input.uv * scale;
    float row = floor(bUV.y);
    float offset = frac(row * 0.5);
    bUV.x += offset;
    float2 fUV = frac(bUV);

    float mortarX = 0.05;
    float mortarY = 0.1;
    bool isMortar = (fUV.x < mortarX) || (fUV.x > 1.0 - mortarX) ||
                    (fUV.y < mortarY) || (fUV.y > 1.0 - mortarY);

    float3 brickCol = float3(0.7, 0.2, 0.1);
    float3 mortarCol = float3(0.7, 0.7, 0.7);
    float3 baseCol = isMortar ? mortarCol : brickCol;

    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float diffuse = max(0.0, dot(N, L));
    float factor = 0.4 + 0.6 * diffuse;
    float3 finalCol = baseCol * factor;

    return float4(finalCol, 1.0);
}

struct PSInput {

{

    float3 V = normalize(cameraPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float NdotV = max(dot(N, V), 0.0);

    float3 col;
    if (NdotV < 0.5)
    {

        col.g = 2.0 * NdotV;
        col.b = 0.0;
    }
    else

        col.r = 1.0 - t;
        col.g = 1.0 - t;
        col.b = t;
    }

    return float4(col, 1.0);

cbuffer UBO : register(b0) {
    float4x4 model;

};

struct PSInput {
    [[vk::location(0)]] float3 worldPos : TEXCOORD0;
    [[vk::location(1)]] float3 normal   : TEXCOORD1;
    [[vk::location(2)]] float2 uv       : TEXCOORD2;
    [[vk::location(3)]] float3 tangent  : TEXCOORD3;
    [[vk::location(4)]] float3 color    : TEXCOORD4;
};

float4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target0
{
    float3 N = normalize(input.normal);
    float3 L = normalize(lightPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float3 V = normalize(cameraPos.xyz - input.worldPos);
    float3 R = reflect(-L, N);

    float3 ambient  = float3(0.1, 0.05, 0.05);
    float  diff     = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    float3 diffuse  = input.color * diff;
    float  spec     = pow(max(dot(R, V), 0.0), 32.0);
    float3 specular = float3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) * spec;

    float3 result = ambient + diffuse + specular;
    result = clamp(result, 0.0, 1.0);

    return float4(result, 1.0);

layout(location = 0) in vec3 worldPos;
layout(location = 1) in vec3 normal;
layout(location = 2) in vec2 uv;
layout(location = 3) in vec3 tangent;

    mat4 view;
    mat4 projection;
    vec4 lightPos;
    vec4 cameraPos;

layout(location = 0) out vec4 outColor;

void main() {
    vec3 N = normalize(normal);
    vec3 L = normalize(ubo.lightPos.xyz - worldPos);
    float diffuse = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    float shade = 0.4 + 0.6 * diffuse;

    vec2 scaledUV = uv * vec2(8.0, 16.0);
    float row = floor(scaledUV.y);
    float stagger = mod(row, 2.0) * 0.5;
    vec2 brickCoord = fract(vec2(scaledUV.x + stagger, scaledUV.y));

    float mortarX = 0.05;
    float mortarY = 0.1;

    vec3 brickColor = vec3(0.7, 0.2, 0.1);
    vec3 mortarColor = vec3(0.7, 0.7, 0.7);

    vec3 baseColor;
    if (brickCoord.x < mortarX || brickCoord.x > (1.0 - mortarX) ||
        brickCoord.y < mortarY || brickCoord.y > (1.0 - mortarY)) {
        baseColor = mortarColor;
    } else {
        baseColor = brickColor;
    }

    vec3 finalColor = baseColor * shade;
    outColor = vec4(finalColor, 1.0);
}

    vec3 specular = vec3(1.0) * pow(max(dot(R, V), 0.0), 32.0);

You are writing a SPIR-V fragment shader as raw binary data, encoded as a hex string.
The binary will be decoded from hex, validated with spirv-val, and rendered on a unit sphere.

**SPIR-V Binary Format (little-endian 32-bit words):**
Each 32-bit word is 8 hex characters (little-endian byte order).

Header (5 words):
```
03022307 // Magic number 0x07230203 (little-endian)
00000100 // Version 1.0 (0x00010000)
00000000 // Generator (0 = manual)
BBBBBBBB // Bound (max ID + 1)
00000000 // Reserved
```

Instructions follow as: first word = (WordCount << 16) | Opcode, then operands.

**Key opcodes (decimal):**
- OpCapability (17): word_count=2, operand=capability (1=Shader)
- OpExtInstImport (11): result_id, name_string
- OpMemoryModel (14): word_count=3, addressing=0(Logical), model=1(GLSL450)
- OpEntryPoint (15): execution_model=4(Fragment), entry_id, name, interface_vars...
- OpExecutionMode (16): entry_id, mode=7(OriginUpperLeft)
- OpDecorate (71): target, decoration, operands
- OpTypeVoid (19), OpTypeFunction (33), OpTypeFloat (22), OpTypeVector (23)
- OpTypePointer (32), OpVariable (59), OpConstant (43)
- OpFunction (54), OpFunctionEnd (56), OpLabel (248)
- OpLoad (61), OpStore (62), OpReturn (253)
- OpCompositeConstruct (80), OpCompositeExtract (81)
- OpDot (148), OpFMul (133), OpFAdd (129), OpFSub (131), OpFNegate (127)
- OpExtInst (12): GLSL.std.450 ext instructions

**Decoration values:** Location=30, DescriptorSet=34, Binding=33, Block=2, Offset=35

**Available inputs (from vertex shader):**
```
location 0: vec3 worldPos
location 1: vec3 normal
location 2: vec2 uv
location 3: vec3 tangent
location 4: vec3 color
```

the raw bytes of the .spv file.

Typical Prompt:
Write a GLSL compute shader for gravitational N-body simulation.

**GLSL Compute Shader Interface:**

```
#version 450

layout(local_size_x = 256) in;

// Each body is stored as two consecutive vec4s:
// vec4(position.xyz, mass)
// vec4(velocity.xyz, 0.0)
// So body i starts at index i*2 in the buffer.

layout(set = 0, binding = 0) readonly buffer InputBodies {
vec4 inData[]; // length = N * 2
};

layout(set = 0, binding = 1) buffer OutputBodies {
vec4 outData[]; // length = N * 2
};

layout(set = 0, binding = 2) uniform Params {
uvec4 counts; // counts.x = N (number of bodies)
vec4 physics; // physics.x = dt, physics.y = softening, physics.z = G
};
```

**Task:** Write a compute shader that performs ONE timestep of gravitational
N-body simulation using the leapfrog/Euler integration method. Each invocation
handles one body (gl_GlobalInvocationID.x), reading its position and velocity
from inData and writing updated values to outData. The acceleration should be
computed from all other bodies using:

acc += G * mass_j * (pos_j - pos_i) / (|pos_j - pos_i|^2 + softening^2)^(3/2)

Velocity is advanced by acc * dt and position is advanced by vel * dt. The
shader will be dispatched ceil(N/256) workgroups in X and run multiple times
with ping-pong buffers for the required number of timesteps.

**Critical Requirements:**
- Guard against gl_GlobalInvocationID.x >= N
- Use the softening parameter to avoid singularities
- Skip self-interaction (i == j)
- Write BOTH position+mass and velocity vec4s to output

Test 47: Hash Mining / Proof of Work (WGSL Compute) Score: 4.00 / 5
Typical Prompt:
Write a WGSL compute shader for hash mining (proof-of-work).

**WGSL Compute Shader Interface:**

```wgsl
@group(0) @binding(0) var baseData : array;
@group(0) @binding(1) var result : array;
@group(0) @binding(2) var params : vec4;
// params.x = difficulty, params.y = range_start, params.z = range_size

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn main(@builtin(global_invocation_id) gid : vec3) { ... }
```

**Task:** Write a compute shader that searches for a uint32 nonce such that
the custom hash of (baseData XOR nonce) has at least `difficulty` trailing
zero bits in the 64-bit output.

**Hash function (MUST match exactly):**
```
function custom_hash(data[16], nonce) -> (h0, h1):
state[0..15] = data[0..15]
for i in 0..15: state[i] ^= (nonce + i)

// 8 rounds of quarter-round mixing (ChaCha-like)
repeat 8 times:
for each group of 4 consecutive elements (i, i+1, i+2, i+3):
a += b; d ^= a; d = rotl(d, 16)
c += d; b ^= c; b = rotl(b, 12)
a += b; d ^= a; d = rotl(d, 8)
c += d; b ^= c; b = rotl(b, 7)

// Fold 16 words to 2:
h0 = state[0] ^ state[2] ^ state[4] ^ state[6] ^ state[8] ^ state[10] ^ state[12] ^ state[14]
h1 = state[1] ^ state[3] ^ state[5] ^ state[7] ^ state[9] ^ state[11] ^ state[13] ^ state[15]
return (h0, h1) // h0 is low 32 bits
```

**Trailing zero count:** Count trailing zero bits of the 64-bit value [h0 | (h1 << 32)].
That is, count from h0's LSB first; if h0 == 0, add 32 and continue counting from h1.

**Algorithm:**
1. Each thread computes: my_nonce = params.y + gid.x (range_start + thread ID)
2. Guard: if gid.x >= params.z, return (out of range)
3. Compute hash, count trailing zeros
4. If trailing_zeros >= difficulty:
Write result[0]=1u, result[1]=nonce, result[2]=h0, result[3]=h1
(Race writes are acceptable - any valid nonce will be verified on CPU)

**Important WGSL notes:**
- Use `var state : array` for the mutable hash state.
- WGSL rotation: `(x << shift) | (x >> (32u - shift))` — all values must be u32.
- The inner quarter-round loop MUST be unrolled (write out all 4 groups
of state[0..3], state[4..7], state[8..11], state[12..15] explicitly).
- Do NOT use atomics. Plain stores to result[] are sufficient.
- All integer literals must be typed: use `0u`, `1u`, `16u`, `32u` etc.

The shader will be dispatched with ceil(range_size / 256) workgroups.
Only ONE dispatch is performed - find the nonce in a single pass.

Test 48: 2D Fluid Simulation - Lattice Boltzmann (SPIR-V ASM Compute) Score: 0.00 / 5
Typical Prompt:
Write a SPIR-V assembly compute shader for 2D Lattice Boltzmann fluid simulation.

**SPIR-V Assembly Compute Shader Interface:**

The shader uses the D2Q9 Lattice Boltzmann model for 2D fluid simulation.

**D2Q9 velocity directions (index k -> (cx, cy)):**
```
k=0: ( 0, 0) w=4/9 (rest)
k=1: ( 1, 0) w=1/9 (east)
k=2: ( 0, 1) w=1/9 (north)
k=3: (-1, 0) w=1/9 (west)
k=4: ( 0,-1) w=1/9 (south)
k=5: ( 1, 1) w=1/36 (NE)
k=6: (-1, 1) w=1/36 (NW)
k=7: (-1,-1) w=1/36 (SW)
k=8: ( 1,-1) w=1/36 (SE)
```

**Buffer layout:**
- Binding 0 (storage, read-only): float array, length W*H*9
Index = (y * W + x) * 9 + k
- Binding 1 (storage, read-write): float array, length W*H*9 (output, NOT writeonly)
- Binding 2 (uniform): { uvec4(W, H, 0, 0), vec4(omega, 0, 0, 0) }

**Algorithm (per cell at gl_GlobalInvocationID.xy):**
Compute one LBM step (collision + streaming) for each lattice cell. Guard against
out-of-bounds (x >= W or y >= H). For the cell distributions f[0..8], compute
macroscopic density rho and velocity (ux, uy) using the D2Q9 directions. Apply
the BGK collision update with:

cu = cx[k]*ux + cy[k]*uy
feq = w[k] * rho * (1 + 3*cu + 4.5*cu*cu - 1.5*(ux*ux + uy*uy))
f_out = f[k] + omega * (feq - f[k])

Then stream each f_out to the neighbor cell (x+cx[k], y+cy[k]) with periodic
wraparound in both axes. Write to the output buffer at the corresponding
neighbor index for k.

**SPIR-V requirements:**
- OpCapability Shader
- OpExecutionMode with LocalSize 16 16 1
- Use gl_GlobalInvocationID for (x, y)
- Declare runtime arrays for storage buffers with OpDecorate ArrayStride 4
- Use OpSMod or manual modulo for periodic boundary conditions


**Test Configurations:**

Subpass 1: 64x64 grid, 100 steps, viscosity=0.1, omega=1.2500

Subpass 3: 128x128 grid, 200 steps, viscosity=0.05, omega=1.5385
Subpass 4: 256x256 grid, 200 steps, viscosity=0.02, omega=1.7857

Write the complete SPIR-V assembly text (starting with "; SPIR-V").
The shader performs ONE LBM step (collision + streaming). It will be
dispatched repeatedly for the required number of timesteps with ping-pong buffers.

Test 49: Parallel Prefix Sum (SPIR-V Binary Compute) Score: 0.00 / 5
Typical Prompt:
Write a SPIR-V binary compute shader (hex-encoded) for parallel inclusive prefix sum.

**SPIR-V Binary (hex-encoded) Compute Shader Interface:**

You must produce raw SPIR-V binary encoded as a hex string (no spaces, no 0x prefix).
The binary must start with the SPIR-V magic number 0x07230203.

**Required layout:**
```
Binding 0 (set=0): Storage buffer (read-only) - uint array, length N
Binding 1 (set=0): Storage buffer (read-write) - uint array, length N
Binding 2 (set=0): Uniform buffer - uint4: [N, 0, 0, 0]

Local size: 256 x 1 x 1
```

**Algorithm:** Inclusive prefix sum (scan)
- Input: [a0, a1, a2, a3, ...]
- Output: [a0, a0+a1, a0+a1+a2, a0+a1+a2+a3, ...]

Compute an inclusive scan over the input array. For N <= 256, use a shared-memory
scan within a single workgroup (synchronize as needed). For N > 256, a naive
fallback (each thread sums all previous elements) is acceptable but slow; full
marks require a multi-workgroup scan.

**SPIR-V binary encoding notes:**
- Little-endian uint32 words
- Magic: 0x07230203
- Version: 0x00010000 (1.0)
- Bound: upper bound on all IDs used + 1
- Schema: 0
- OpCapability Shader = [0x00020011, 0x00000001]
- OpMemoryModel Logical GLSL450 = [0x00030006, 0x00000001, 0x00000001]
- OpEntryPoint GLCompute = opcode 0x0000000F, execution model 5
- OpExecutionMode LocalSize = opcode 0x00000010, mode 17 (LocalSize)
- OpDecorate Binding = decoration 33
- OpDecorate DescriptorSet = decoration 34
- OpDecorate ArrayStride = decoration 6
- OpDecorate BufferBlock or Block = decoration 2 or 3
- OpTypeInt 32 0 = unsigned int
- OpTypePointer StorageBuffer = storage class 12
- OpVariable StorageBuffer = storage class 12

Encode every uint32 word as exactly 8 hex characters (little-endian).


**Test Configurations:**
Subpass 0: N=256 elements
Subpass 1: N=1,024 elements
Subpass 2: N=4,096 elements
Subpass 3: N=16,384 elements
Subpass 4: N=65,536 elements

Provide the complete SPIR-V binary as a hex string.
Each uint32 word must be 8 hex digits, little-endian byte order.
The entire binary is one continuous hex string with no spaces or line breaks.

Typical Prompt:
Write a GLSL compute shader for 3D boid flocking simulation.

**GLSL Compute Shader Interface:**

```glsl
#version 450

layout(local_size_x = 256) in;

// Each boid stored as two vec4s: [pos.xyz, 0], [vel.xyz, 0]
// Boid i is at index i*2 and i*2+1
layout(set = 0, binding = 0) readonly buffer InputBoids {
vec4 inData[]; // length = N * 2
};

layout(set = 0, binding = 1) buffer OutputBoids {
vec4 outData[]; // length = N * 2
};

layout(set = 0, binding = 2) uniform Params {
uvec4 counts; // counts.x = N
vec4 radii; // radii.x=dt, radii.y=sepRadius, radii.z=alignRadius, radii.w=cohRadius
vec4 weights; // weights.x=sepWeight, weights.y=alignWeight, weights.z=cohWeight, weights.w=maxSpeed
vec4 bounds; // bounds.x=boundSize, bounds.y=boundForce
};
```

**Task:** Write a compute shader that performs ONE timestep of 3D boid
flocking simulation (Reynolds' rules). Each invocation handles one boid
(gl_GlobalInvocationID.x), reading its position/velocity from inData and
writing updated values to outData. Use separation/align/cohesion with the
provided radii and weights, average neighbor contributions, and apply the
boundary force when a component exceeds boundSize*0.4 (push toward center
using boundForce and boundSize*0.5 scaling). Update velocity by accel*dt,
clamp speed to maxSpeed, then update position by vel*dt.

**Critical Requirements:**
- Guard against gl_GlobalInvocationID.x >= N
- Skip self (i == j) and zero-distance neighbors
- Average the accumulated forces by neighbor count (avoid division by zero)
- Clamp velocity magnitude to maxSpeed


**Flocking Parameters (constant across all subpasses):**
Separation radius: 2.0, weight: 1.5
Alignment radius: 5.0, weight: 1.0
Cohesion radius: 8.0, weight: 1.0
Max speed: 5.0
Bound size: 50.0, bound force: 0.5

properties. If GPS altitude is dropping, radar altitude is stable, and barometric
altitude is climbing - two failures have occured, and you have to pick wisely.

brush up on your knowledge of stalls, asymetric thurst, yaw dampening, and trim.
5. Vne is (~365 KIAS / Mach 0.82).

previous values, etc. They persist across calls within a scenario.

Key facts:
- Wheel speed sensors (4): FL, FR, RL, RR in km/h. Any can fail.
- Gyroscopes (3): yaw rate in degrees/second. Any can fail silently.
- Accelerometers (3): longitudinal and lateral in m/s². Any can fail.
- GPS (2): position in meters, speed in km/h. Can lose signal.
- Lidar (12 beams): range in meters at angles from -90° to +90°.
- Vision (3 independent systems): lane line distances, types (solid/dashed),
obstacle detection (bool + distance + relative speed), speed limit signs,
lane offset, road curvature. ANY can fail or flicker!
- `estimated_mu`: estimated tire-road friction (1.0=dry, <0.3=ice).
- `target_speed_kmh`: desired speed. `target_lane`: desired lane (0-2).
- `*_valid` flags exist but may be WRONG on failed sensors.
- Sensors can FLICKER: randomly return invalid data for a few frames.

**Output:** Return a dict:
```
steering: -1.0 (full left) to +1.0 (full right)
0.0 = straight ahead
throttle: 0.0 (no power) to 1.0 (full power)
brake: 0.0 (no brake) to 1.0 (emergency stop)
```
If you omit a key, the current value is maintained.

**Critical Design Requirements:**
1. **Sensor fusion**: Cross-check redundant sensors. Median/voting for disagreements.
2. **Lane keeping**: Stay centered in lane using vision line distances and lidar.
3. **Speed control**: Maintain target speed, respect speed limits.
4. **Obstacle avoidance**: If obstacle detected, brake and/or lane change.
5. **Traction management**: On low-mu surfaces, reduce speed, gentler inputs.
6. **Graceful degradation**: Handle sensor failures, flickering data.
7. **Persistence**: Module-level variables persist across calls for filtering/PID.

**Test Scenarios (25 total):**
0. Normal highway cruise
1. Gentle curve
2. Slow vehicle ahead
3. Emergency stop — stopped vehicle
4. Cut-in from adjacent lane
5. Ice patch — reduced traction
6. Aquaplaning — very low friction

8. Two wheel speed sensors fail
9. Gyro sensor failure

11. Vision system 1 failure
12. All vision systems flickering
13. Front lidar beams fail

15. Total brake failure
16. Throttle stuck at 30%
17. Road debris
18. Dense traffic
19. Crosswind gust
20. Steering partially jammed
21. Ice + stopped vehicle
22. Flickering sensors in curve
23. Reduced visibility
24. Multi-failure + obstacle

Test 53: Spacecraft Orbital Docking Autopilot (Python) Score: 0.00 / 25
Typical Prompt:
Write a Python autopilot to dock a spacecraft with a space station in orbit.

**CRITICAL ORBITAL MECHANICS INSIGHT:**
In orbit, relative motion is COUNTER-INTUITIVE:
- Thrusting TOWARD the target (prograde if behind) raises your orbit → you SLOW DOWN relative to target
- To catch up: thrust RETROGRADE (backward!) to lower orbit → you go FASTER
- Radial thrusts cause oscillation, not direct movement
- Cross-track corrections require thrusts at specific orbital positions
- Near the target (<50m), approximate as linear (CW equations work)
- Far away (>200m), full orbital mechanics dominate

**Function Signature:**
```python
def autopilot_step(state: dict, dt: float) -> dict:
```

Key sensor notes:
- Relative position/velocity in LVLH frame: x=radial (up), y=along-track (velocity dir), z=cross-track
- NEGATIVE y = behind station (most common start). Must CLOSE the y gap.
- Range finders give scalar distance. Radar/lidar give 3D relative pos/vel.
- All sensors can fail silently! Cross-check redundant sensors.
- Docking camera only active within 500m. Gives bearing to docking port.
- Ground station data updates every ~30s (stale but reliable).

**Output:** Return a dict:
```
thrust_x: -1.0 to +1.0 (radial: + = away from Earth)
thrust_y: -1.0 to +1.0 (along-track: + = prograde)
thrust_z: -1.0 to +1.0 (cross-track: + = north)
att_rate_roll: rad/s (max ±0.035)
att_rate_pitch: rad/s (max ±0.035)
att_rate_yaw: rad/s (max ±0.035)
```
Each thrust axis: 220N per thruster, Isp=290s. Fuel is LIMITED (~500 kg).

**Docking Success Criteria:**
- Range < 2m AND relative speed < 0.3 m/s

**Approach Strategy Hints:**
1. Far (>200m): Use Hohmann-like transfer — retrograde to lower orbit if behind
2. Medium (50-200m): Gentle corrections, V-bar approach preferred
3. Close (<50m): Linear regime, direct thrust corrections OK
4. Final (<10m): Very gentle, < 0.1 m/s approach speed

**Test Scenarios (25 total):**
0. V-bar approach — 200m behind
1. V-bar approach — 500m behind
2. V-bar close approach — 50m
3. R-bar approach — 200m below
4. Approach from above — 200m
5. Cross-track offset — 100m
6. Ahead of station — 200m
7. Diagonal — 150m radial + 150m along-track
8. Long-range — 2km behind
9. Drifting away — 200m with 0.5 m/s radial
10. Closing too fast — 2 m/s approach
11. Range sensor 1 failed
12. Radar relative position failed
13. Gyro 1 bias + gyro 2 drift
14. Star tracker 1 dead
15. Both GPS receivers failed
16. Docking camera failed
17. Uncommanded +Y thrust (0.5N)
18. Uncommanded cross-track thrust
19. Flickering range + radar sensors
20. Low fuel — only 50 kg remaining
21. Cross-track + radar failure
22. Higher orbit — 450km
23. All range sensors very noisy
24. Multi-failure + uncommanded thrust + offset

**ILS Approach Key Concepts:**
- `glideslope_N_dots`: deviation from 3° glideslope (+above/-below), 3 receivers
- `localizer_N_dots`: deviation from runway centerline (+right/-left), 3 receivers
- `radio_alt_ft`: height above ground (critical for flare)
- `dme_N_nm`: distance to runway threshold
- `weight_on_wheels`: True when landed
- `target_vref_kt`: reference approach speed (typically 137kt)
- `decision_height_ft`: minimum altitude to continue approach (200ft CAT I)
- Elevator command 0 = trimmed flight. Positive = pitch up.

**Output:** Return a dict with any of:
```
elevator: -1.0 (nose down) to +1.0 (nose up), relative to trim
aileron: -1.0 (roll left) to +1.0 (roll right)
rudder: -1.0 (yaw left) to +1.0 (yaw right)
throttle_1: 0.0 to 1.0 (left engine)
throttle_2: 0.0 to 1.0 (right engine)
elevator_trim: -1.0 to +1.0
flaps: degrees (0-40)
gear: 0.0 (up) or 1.0 (down)
speedbrake: 0.0 (retracted) to 1.0 (full)
spoiler: 0.0 or 1.0 (ground spoilers, deploy after touchdown)
autobrake: 0.0 to 1.0 (braking force after touchdown)
reverse_1: 0.0 to 1.0 (left engine reverse thrust)
reverse_2: 0.0 to 1.0 (right engine reverse thrust)
```

**Approach Phases:**
1. **Intercept** (>1000ft): Track glideslope and localizer, configure for landing
2. **Approach** (1000ft-200ft): Stabilise on glideslope, speed, config
3. **Flare** (<50ft radio alt): Reduce descent rate, idle thrust
4. **Touchdown & Rollout**: Deploy spoilers, reverse thrust, autobrake

**Go-Around:**
If the approach is unstable or unsafe, abort the landing:
- Apply TOGA thrust (throttle 1.0), pitch up, retract speedbrake
- Climb to 1500ft AGL — this completes the go-around
- The sim will then **restart** from a stable approach position with the
**same failures and weather**. Your autopilot must land on the retry.
- Each go-around costs a **0.1 point penalty** on a perfect landing.
- After **10 go-arounds** the scenario fails (score 0.0).

**Scoring:**
- **1.0** — Normal landing: stopped on the runway, or slowed below 50kt
with >30% runway remaining (pilot takes over to taxi).
Minus 0.1 per go-around.
- **0.5** — Hard landing: touchdown vertical speed 360–600 fpm.
Aircraft needs inspection but is reusable, everyone walks away.
- **0.1** — Minor overrun: aircraft rolls off the end but is caught by the
EMAS arrestor bed (within 150m past runway end). Everyone safe,
aircraft damaged.
- **0.0** — Catastrophic: touchdown >600 fpm, major overrun
beyond EMAS, runway excursion, CFIT, or failure to land. Write-off or
loss of life.

**Test Scenarios (25 total):**

2. High on glideslope
3. Low on glideslope
4. Offset from centerline

7. Strong crosswind — 25kt

9. CAT III low visibility
10. Slippery wet runway [Overruns at LGA, MDW]
11. Icy runway

13. Localizer 1 stuck + 2 biased

18. Heavy weight landing

20. Dual engine failure — glide approach [Gimli Glider (1983) / US Airways 1549 (2009)]
21. Missed approach required
22. Severe turbulence on final
23. ILS signal flickering
24. Engine failure + crosswind + wet runway [Multiple incidents]

Your single autopilot function must handle ALL scenarios.
Persistence: module-level variables persist across calls within a scenario,

Typical Prompt:
Write a C++ chess bot that for any given chess position, returns the best move to make (or the best
move you can find before the timeout).

You receive the chess position as a string in FEN notation, and you must return the move in
disambiguated algebraic notation (including the starting square, piece type, and destination square).

See:
- https://www.chess.com/terms/fen-chess

Here is an example FEN representing the starting position with white to move:
```
rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1
```

Here is an example disambiguated algebraic move:
```
pe2e4
```
This represents the king's pawn opening - moving the pawn from e2 to e4.

**Move notation rules:**
- Piece letter (lowercase p for pawn, uppercase N/B/R/Q/K for others) + source square + destination square.
- Use "x" between source and destination for captures: `pe4xd5`
- Promotion: append `/` and the piece letter, e.g. `pe7e8/Q`
- Castling: `O-O` (kingside) or `O-O-O` (queenside).
- En passant: append `ep`, e.g. `pe5xd6ep`
- Check: append `+`, e.g. `Bb4c5+`
- Checkmate: append `#`, e.g. `Qd1h5#`

**Input format (stdin, two lines):**
```
timeout_in_seconds
fen_string
```

**Output format (stdout, one line):**
```
move_in_disambiguated_algebraic
```

timeout_in_seconds will be at least 5. Your code will be compiled with full optimisations and
run on a machine with multiple cores, so threading is encouraged.
